source_review.notes: Checked active NASA-HDBK-1009A (2025); current NASA Systems Engineering Handbook pages for scope, configuration and technical-data management; active NASA-STD-7009B and the current standards index listing NASA-HDBK-7009B (2026); DoDI 5000.97; the DoD Digital Engineering Strategy; final OMG SysML 2.0; and the NIST MBSE publication record. Nine final URLs returned HTTP 200 through direct command-line retrieval. The official DoDI PDF returned HTTP 403 to scripted curl but was independently retrieved through browser access on the review date and checked for lifecycle configuration, real-world updates, intended-use V&V/accreditation and authoritative-source guidance.

numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts concern declared teaching data only and do not establish semantic correctness, rightful ownership, completeness or intended-use credibility.

evidence: Confirmed unique resolution applies per claim, baseline and intended use, permitting federation without duplicate control.

symbolic_recomputation.notes: All relations are explicitly conditional and avoid equating consistency, authority, freshness, generation, verification, validation and acceptance.

invariant_checking.notes: The module rejects both uncontrolled federation and false monoliths: one authority per governed claim is compatible with multiple connected sources.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents governance relations and invariants but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed authoritative, true, correct, consistent, current, complete, fresh, verified, validated, accredited, credible, synchronized, generated, migrated and operational language for bounded scope.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed, and the checker explicitly cannot determine claim correctness, legitimate ownership or real engineering credibility.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked model, element, view, engineering claim, authoritative source, authoritative source of truth, authority map, technical baseline, provenance, semantic consistency, credibility, derived artifact, digital thread and model debt. Authority is consistently treated as a granular socio-technical contract rather than a database property.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked claim inventory, federated ownership, metamodel and identity governance, working/released state, provenance, links, conflict quarantine, access, use-specific credibility, design/observed reconciliation, CI, model-capable reviews, generated products, suppliers, protection, migration and retirement. Examples cover interfaces, federation, review annotation, duplicate requirements, simulation reuse, code generation, supplier delivery, unauthorized edits, telemetry divergence and tool exit.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from authority claims through semantic/configuration control, credibility, collaboration/delivery and lifecycle assurance. Ten examples and five complete solutions require learners to design an authority map, repair a false monolith, qualify a reused degradation model, plan a 12-year semantic migration and investigate model/product conflict without presuming which source is wrong.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, systems-modeling, simulation, configuration-management, data-management, digital-engineering, tool-vendor, supplier, software, safety, security, privacy, legal, records, operations, verification, validation, accreditation, or technical-authority review is claimed.
